_what: The one write of an account's own records (trillion src/own-record-resource.mjs `records:*` -> src/customer-database-records.mjs `write` -> parts/record-log/do-work/record-log-store.mjs `write(records)`). Each item writes one whole root record { id, type, value }: a list (type list), a list's rows (type record:<row_type>, declared by the list), or any other kind declared in record-model.json or by another record; value null removes the record, and a removal may omit type. An optional `expected` condition is checked against the transaction's batch-start logical snapshot: null requires absence, while {type, value} requires that exact existing logical kind and full root value; omission keeps unconditional writes. Any mismatch conflicts the whole command before records, keys or receipts are written. A record id is text without '/'. The engine checks every write against the live record model (record-model.json kinds, lists.json field kinds and the declaring records), seals erasable fields under the record's key, and keeps one count receipt ({changed, write_count}) in the same transaction. `operation` is the command's name at the @own-records resource (POST /records { records } in the browser, run_resource_operation method for an agent). `input_schema` is its admission and receipt schema: `records` is writeOnly, so the command journal keeps the input digest and the permit reference, never a record id or word. `receipt_kinds` are kinds an ordinary record command never writes, by type or by an id <kind>:... (their owner is the command journal). A new writable kind is a row in record-model.json or a list a person makes, never code here.
_compact_expected: expected:{type,identity} compares the existing opaque current root revision/stamp token from a current records:read of this same id and kind, against the transaction's batch-start observation. It does not repeat the old value, parse a number, hash displayed/derived data or fence shared children. expected:{type,value}, null and omission retain their existing meanings. A snapshot with both value and identity requires both conditions. Historical at reads never mint a current identity.

resource_selection._what: One declared record batch is the initial atomic group. Resolve only its explicit identity fields, deduplicate them, and keep all batch identities together; the resource owner applies existing affinity or an installed growth target. No kind/id hashing or splitting is inferred here.

check_only.description: true runs every check and refusal of this write on its transaction, then rolls back: nothing is stored, journaled, copied or announced, and the answer is {changed, write_count, check_only: true} as the write would have counted them, or the refusal the write would have met. Use a fresh request_key: the key is not kept.

scope.description: Complete admitted resource history carried on creation, reads, writes and recovery. Omission selects the account's original namespace; it never finds an arbitrary history. Creation is explicit. Incarnation and generation must match the stored header.

oneOf.description: A readRecord snapshot containing both value and identity requires BOTH to match. Select only type and identity for a compact condition.

identity.description: Opaque current root revision/stamp token from a current records:read of this same id and kind. Compare as text, not a number or content hash. Shared/computed dependencies are not fenced.
